## Comparability note

All five are on the same calendar fiscal-year basis (Jan 1 – Dec 31) for both FY2023 and FY2024, so the year-over-year comparisons are on a like-for-like period basis [DOC-1]. Two caveats before scoring:

- "Strongest performer" is not defined by the source; the ranking changes depending on whether you weight scale/margin, growth rate, or margin expansion.
- The excerpt gives only revenue and operating income. It does not disclose whether any of the revenue growth is organic versus acquisition-driven, nor does it give net income, cash flow, or balance-sheet data — so Alaska's outsized revenue growth in particular cannot be verified as organic from this source.

## FY2024 scorecard

| Airline | Revenue FY23→FY24 | Rev. growth | Op. income FY23→FY24 | Op. income growth | FY24 op. margin | Margin Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $58,048M → $61,643M [DOC-1] | +6.2% | $5,521M → $5,995M [DOC-1] | +8.6% | 9.7% | +0.2 pp |
| United | $53,717M → $57,063M [DOC-1] | +6.2% | $4,211M → $5,096M [DOC-1] | +21.0% | 8.9% | +1.1 pp |
| Southwest | $26,091M → $27,483M [DOC-1] | +5.3% | $224M → $321M [DOC-1] | +43.3% | 1.2% | +0.3 pp |
| American | $52,788M → $54,211M [DOC-1] | +2.7% | $3,034M → $2,614M [DOC-1] | **−13.8%** | 4.8% | −0.9 pp |
| Alaska | $10,426M → $11,735M [DOC-1] | +12.6% | $394M → $570M [DOC-1] | +44.7% | 4.9% | +1.1 pp |

## Interpretation

- **Delta** posted both the largest operating income ($5,995M) and the highest operating margin (9.7%) of the group, on the largest revenue base ($61,643M) [DOC-1]. It grew revenue and profit simultaneously, which is the cleanest signal of strength.
- **United** had the best combination of scale and improvement: +21.0% operating income growth on +6.2% revenue growth, expanding margin 7.8% → 8.9% [DOC-1]. It is the closest challenger and arguably the "most improved."
- **Alaska** and **Southwest** show the highest percentage growth rates, but off much smaller bases — Southwest's +43.3% operating income growth is on just $224M of prior-year profit and still leaves a 1.2% margin, the weakest in the group [DOC-1]. Alaska's +12.6% revenue growth is the fastest, but its 4.9% margin is roughly half Delta's [DOC-1].
- **American** is the clear laggard: the slowest revenue growth (+2.7%) and the only operating income decline (−$420M, to $2,614M) [DOC-1].

On the most defensible composite — absolute profit, profitability rate, and direction of travel — Delta leads. If the criterion were rate of improvement rather than level of profitability, United would rank first.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — highest FY2024 operating income ($5,995M) and highest operating margin (9.7%) among the five, with both revenue and operating income up year over year; United is the runner-up and the fastest-improving large carrier (+21.0% operating income), while American was the weakest (only carrier with declining operating income, −13.8%).
